questions.text: Data Protection Legislation: Legal basis for privacy: (1) Existence of Data Protection Act (GDPR-aligned?); (2) Independent Data Protection Authority (DPA); (3) Enforcement powers of DPA (fines?); (4) Government exemption limits (can state bypass law?); (5) Cross-border data transfer rules; (6) Mandatory breach notification; (7) Judicial oversight.
questions.evidence_required: Data Protection Act, DPA annual report, Court rulings
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many countries passing DPAs, but enforcement is weak. State often exempts itself on 'national security' grounds.

questions.text: Digital Identity Legal Framework: Rules for ID: (1) Mandatory vs Voluntary nature; (2) Consequences of non-registration (denial of services?); (3) Use of ID for surveillance (legal limits); (4) Biometric data collection mandate; (5) Right to be forgotten (if applicable); (6) Linking of databases (legal basis); (7) Discrimination protection.
questions.evidence_required: Digital ID Act, Regulations, Constitutional court judgments
questions.africa_specific_notes: Courts (e.g., in Kenya, Jamaica) have halted ID systems due to lack of legal framework. Law must precede technology.

questions.text: Independent Oversight Mechanisms: Who watches the watchers?: (1) Parliamentary committee oversight; (2) Auditor General audits of ID system; (3) Civil society observation role; (4) Ombudsman for complaints; (5) Judicial review of decisions; (6) Whistleblower protection for officials; (7) Regular impact assessments.
questions.evidence_required: Committee reports, Audit reports, Court cases
questions.africa_specific_notes: Executive branch often pushes ID systems without legislative scrutiny. Independent oversight prevents abuse.

questions.text: Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM): Fixing mistakes: (1) Clear channel for complaints (ID errors, exclusion); (2) Timeline for resolution; (3) Accessibility of GRM (rural/offline); (4) Appeal process; (5) Compensation for errors; (6) Tracking of complaint stats; (7) Independence of GRM.
questions.evidence_required: GRM procedure, Complaint logs, Resolution stats
questions.africa_specific_notes: If your ID has the wrong name/DOB, your life stops. Fixing it can take years without a proper GRM.

questions.text: Inclusion Mandate & Strategy: Leaving no one behind: (1) Strategy for marginalized groups (nomads, border communities); (2) Alternative proof of ID (if no birth cert); (3) Mobile registration units; (4) Affirmative action in registration; (5) Staff training on non-discrimination; (6) Monitoring of exclusion rates; (7) Budget for inclusion.
questions.evidence_required: Inclusion strategy, Registration stats by group, Training materials
questions.africa_specific_notes: Border communities (e.g., Somalis in Kenya, Nubians) often face vetting/discrimination. ID system must not weaponize citizenship.

questions.text: Accessibility Governance: Access for disabled: (1) Physical access to centers; (2) Biometric exception policy (amputees); (3) Website accessibility (WCAG standards); (4) Sign language support; (5) Assistive technology compatibility; (6) Consultation with disability groups; (7) Staff sensitization.
questions.evidence_required: Accessibility audit, Exception policy, Consultation minutes
questions.africa_specific_notes: Blind users need screen readers for e-Gov. Amputees need non-fingerprint options.

questions.text: Data Sovereignty & Vendor Lock-in: Owning the system: (1) State ownership of data; (2) State ownership of source code/IP; (3) Ability to switch vendors; (4) Local hosting requirement; (5) Knowledge transfer clauses; (6) Open standards usage; (7) Exit strategy.
questions.evidence_required: Contract IP clauses, Data hosting location, Exit plan
questions.africa_specific_notes: African nations often 'rent' their ID systems from foreign firms. If they stop paying, the system turns off. Sovereignty is key.

questions.text: Algorithmic Accountability: Governing AI: (1) Policy on AI use in government; (2) Human oversight requirements; (3) Impact assessment for automated decisions; (4) Ban on certain uses (e.g., social scoring); (5) Public register of algorithms; (6) Ethical AI guidelines; (7) Liability for AI errors.
questions.evidence_required: AI policy, Impact assessments, Ethical guidelines
questions.africa_specific_notes: AI adoption is early but risky. Preventing 'black box' government decisions is a governance priority.

scoring_notes: Layer 3 (Governance) for Government in SSA: Legal protection (DPA) and Inclusion are the pillars. Without them, ID systems become tools of exclusion and surveillance.
